summary: The root قبس (qbs) primarily means to take or acquire fire from a source. This concept extends metaphorically to acquiring knowledge or catching a fever from someone else.
lane: 1 قَبَسَ نَارًا ذ , aor. قَبِسَ , (Msb, K,) inf. n. قَبْسٌ , (T, K,) He took fire, مِنْهُ [ from him; ] (K;) as also : (S, K:) or he took fire from the main mass thereof; (Msb;) as also [alone]. (Msb, K.) -b2- [Hence,] قَبَسَ عِلْمًا , (and مِنَ العِلْمِ , TA,) (assumed tropical:) He acquired knowledge, مِنْهُ [ from him; ] (Ks, K, TA;) as also : (Ks, S, K, TA:) or he learned knowledge; as also . (Msb.) -b3- [Hence also, قَبَسَ حُمَّى (assumed tropical:) He caught a fever from another; as also .] You say, هٰذِهِ حُمَّى قَبْسٍ (assumed tropical:) This is a fever caught from another; not accidentally inbred: (A, TA:) but Sgh explains it differently, as signifying an accidental fever. (TA.) And الحُمَّى مِنْ غَيْرِهِ وَلَمْ تَعْرِضْ لَهُ مِنْ نَفْسِهِ (assumed tropical:) [ He caught the fever from another; and it did not accidentally come to him from himself ]. (A, TA.) -A2- قَبَسَ مِنْهُ نَارًا , aor. قَبِسَ , inf. n. قَبْسٌ , [ He sought from him fire; (see its part. n., below;)] (S;) [and so , for اقتبس مِنْهُ نَارًا ; for you say,] اِقْتَبَسْنَا فُلَانًا فَأَبَى ان يُقْبِسَنَا , meaning, [ We sought fire from such a one, and he refused ] to give us fire. (TA.) -b2- [And hence, قَبَسَ عِلْمًا (assumed tropical:) He sought knowledge; (see, again, its part. n., below;) and so ; as appears from an explanation of the part. n. of this latter also; and from the saying,] أَتَانَا فُلَانٌ يَقْتَبِسُ العِلْمَ فَأَقْبَسْنَاهُ , meaning, (assumed tropical:) [ Such a one came to us seeking knowledge, and ] we taught him. (TA.) -A3- Also, قَبَسَ النَّارَ He lighted, or kindled, the fire. (IKtt.) -A4- See also 4, passim.

headwords.def: قَبَسَ نَارًا , aor. قَبِسَ, (Msb, K,) inf. n. قَبْسٌ, (T, K,) He took fire, مِنْهُ [ from him; ] (K;) as also: (S, K:) or he took fire from the main mass thereof; (Msb;) as also [alone]. (Msb, K.) [Hence,] قَبَسَ عِلْمًا, (and مِنَ العِلْمِ, TA,) (assumed tropical:) He acquired knowledge, مِنْهُ [ from him; ] (Ks, K, TA;) as also: (Ks, S, K, TA:) or he learned knowledge; as also.

He gave him a قَبَس [a brand, or burning stick, or burning piece of fire-wood ]: (S, K:) or he gave him fire: and he brought him fire: (TA:) and اقبسهُ نَارًا (Ks, S, Msb) he gave him fire; (S, * Msb, TA;) as also نَارًا.

Fire: (TA:) or a live coal: (Bd, xx. 10:) or [more commonly, and more properly, like نَفَضٌ in the sense of مَنْفُوضٌ;] a firebrand ( شُعْلَةٌ مِنْ نَارٍ, T, S, A, Msb, K, * and Bd ubi supra,) taken from the main mass of fire; (T, A, Msb, * K;) as also and (A) and: (S, A, Msb, K:) the last two [properly] signify a thing [ such as a stick, or piece of fire-wood, ] with which one has taken fire: (TA:) and قَبَسٌ is also explained as signifying a live coal, or piece of fire, ( جِ ْوَةٌ…

[inf. n. of un. of 1; A single act of taking fire; &c. Hence the saying,] مَا زُرْتُكَ إِلَّا كَقَبْسَةِ العَجْلَانِ [ I did not visit thee save like the hasty person's single act of taking fire ]. (TA.) See also قَبَسٌ.

[act. part. n. of 1; Taking fire; a taker of fire; &c. Hence the saying,] مَا أَنْتَ إِلَّا كالقَابِسِ العَجْلَانِ [ Thou art none other than like the hasty taker of fire ]. (A.) [ (assumed tropical:) Acquiring, or learning, knowledge; an acquirer, or a learner, of knowledge. ] Seeking, or a seeker of, fire: pl. أَقْبَاسٌ; its only broken pl. (TA.) (assumed tropical:) Seeking, or a seeker of, knowledge; as also. (TA.) القَوَابِسُ [pl. of القَابِسُ, like as الفَوَارِسُ is pl.

The place of the fire-brand: i. e., firewood that has been lighted: or charcoal that has become hard; opposed to حُمَمَةٌ, which is [a piece of] charcoal that does not hold together: pl. مَقَابِسُ. (Msb.)
A sort of طُنْبُور: see مَعَازِفُ.

headword_note: Lane organises by verb form and principal noun, not by every inflected form. A word with no headword entry falls back to the root meaning; nothing is inferred.
